Rules / Modernization

SK1020 Use ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull

⚠ Retired. The id stays allocated for ever because every baseline in every repository names it (ADR-012), and the analyzer no longer enables it, so nothing new is reported. The page is here so that an old finding can still be looked up.

A hand-written null guard that ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull already is.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since0.6

Why

⚠ Retired (#281). CA1510 is enabled by default at Info in a stock SDK build and reports all three of this rule's positive fixtures with nothing configured, which is the same visibility this rule shipped at (suggestion). ADR-008 is host, never rebuild, so the rule is withdrawn rather than kept as a second opinion. The id stays allocated for ever (ADR-012). The BCL helper is one line instead of three, captures the argument expression itself through CallerArgumentExpression so the message cannot drift from the parameter name, and is annotated so the nullable analysis knows the argument is non-null afterwards — which the hand-written form only manages when the throw is the whole if body.

Example

Instead of:

if (source is null) {
    throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(source));
}

Write:

ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(source);

When it does not fire

Requires System.ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull to exist in the compilation, so a project on an older target framework is silent rather than offered an uncompilable fix. Only fires when the guard is an if whose condition is exactly x is null or x == null (with the same operator-== check SK1010 makes) and whose body is exactly one throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(x)) with no message argument and no other statement — a guard that also logs, or that throws a derived exception, or that passes a custom message, is a deliberate choice and is left alone.

Configuration
